scenario: three valid calls: (a) no-query baseline, (b) query with a word absent from any event ('marriage relationship events'), (c) query with a word present in events ('stammering')

result_summary.note: confirms all 64 life_events for native chart are reachable with no query filter

AND-semantics ILIKE search requires every whitespace-split word to match somewhere in description/domain/category/event_type/source_citation for a row. The word 'events' (generic, not present in any life_events row) makes the whole AND-query match nothing, even though a genuinely on-topic row exists (category=relationship, domain=relationship/romantic_long_term_started, description mentions 'wife (married 2013-12-11)').

correctly returns the 2 stammering-related life events (congenital-onset correction row + original 1995 three-phase-arc row) — confirms the ILIKE AND-search mechanism does work correctly when query words are actually present in the corpus.

mechanism_trace.note: Comment at line 145 (tag 'WP-B1 F-LEL-NOOP') documents that `query` used to be a complete no-op (forwarded but never read) and was deliberately fixed to an AND-semantics case-insensitive ILIKE substring search across 5 text columns, split on whitespace, 'so a non-matching query honestly narrows to zero rows instead of silently ignoring the filter'. This is working as designed — not a defect — but the tool's declared param description ('Natural language life-event query') overstates the actual mechanism, which is a strict literal-substring AND match, not semantic/NL understanding. A multi-word natural-language phrase like a caller might plausibly type ('marriage relationship events') can honestly return zero hits even when clearly relevant events exist, simply because one incidental word (here 'events') isn't in the corpus text.
